summary: 1946 two-story prototype lookout cab on Flattop Mountain, Gifford Pinchot National Forest; dismantled and moved to a center near Entiat, Washington; the summit holds no lookout cab now.

facts.design: Two-story prototype cab with slanted windows and curved hip roof (1946)
facts.status_note: The 2005 sources say the FFLA dismantled the cab and relocated it to the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center near Entiat; the center describes its current structure as a replica of the top story, built partly from the lookout's old wood.

access.note: Drive-up on forest roads. Rocky road; good tires are advised. No lookout cab remains on the summit.

visit.trail_note: Summit reached by forest roads; use FR 8821 for access. The last mile is rocky.

corrections.why: The 1946 cab was dismantled and moved to the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center; the 1996 NHLR entry predates that, and the FFLOS entry says the tower was disassembled.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives a 12 by 12 foot cab; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb give 14 by 14 feet. Not resolved; both figures are shown in the story.
firelookout.com dates the 16 by 20 foot frame house to about 1921; WillhiteWeb dates it to 1922. Both agree it moved to the west end in 1930.
The FFLOS register says the tower was disassembled by 2025. firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb date the dismantling and move to 2005. The story reports both and does not choose.
The NHLR entry (registered 1996) describes a standing lookout. Later histories show the cab was moved away from the summit.

notes_for_editor: The record us-wa-flattop-mountain carries the 2026 FFLOS entry (US 171, WA 507). A separate record us-wa-flattop (Flattop Lookout Site, FFLOS 2012, US 1315 WA 215, gone) appears to describe the same summit. Editor should consider a merge. Built date: the 1946 year comes from firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb; the NHLR entry gives no built year. Cab size conflicts (12 vs 14 feet). Replica status: the CBFIC page calls its structure a replica of the top story, built partly from the old wood; a search snippet also mentions a dispute over whether it is a moved original, but that claim was not read and is not used. The Mount Adams lookout is a separate structure and is not covered here. WillhiteWeb's 'Location Today' note describes the summit without a date, so the current condition is dated only to that visit. CBFIC hours and visitor access were not verified; the story gives no hours and does not recommend a visit. The register's 2005 visit report is the only source for that year's condition. The record's kind two_story describes the original summit cab; the CBFIC replica is one story. No new photos.
